fatal_errors: The baseline incorrectly assigns >50% room-temperature ductility to HfMoTaTiZr; that value belongs to HfNbTaTiZr, whereas as-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a fracture strain of approximately 11.6%.
The proposed V substitution does not reconstruct the demonstrated intervention of adding 4.2 at.% Cr to form approximately 4 vol.% reticulated Laves phase.
The cited evidence does not show that replacing Hf with V preserves either the approximately 1600 MPa room-temperature strength or approximately 855 MPa elevated-temperature strength of HfMoTaTiZr.
explanation: The proposal addresses the density–strength problem and offers a distinct, chemically plausible lightweighting strategy, since V is much lighter than Hf. However, it misses the target intervention, structural mediator, and dual mechanism: Cr addition, lattice contraction/solid-solution hardening, and crack hindrance by an interconnected Cr2(Ti,Zr,Hf,Ta) Laves network. Its mechanical baseline is materially corrupted by transferring the >50% ductility of HfNbTaTiZr to HfMoTaTiZr. The evidence only supports the general use of lower-density refractory elements and does not validate Hf-to-V substitution, retained phase constitution, or retained high-temperature properties. The controlled composition series and numerical rejection thresholds are useful, but tensile tests are not directly comparable to the target room-temperature compression results, strain rate is unspecified, and the experiment lacks phase morphology, phase fraction, lattice-parameter, and dislocation-density measurements needed to test the stated mechanism. The rule that failure of any substituted composition falsifies the entire strategy is also overly strong; failure at 30% replacement would not rule out success at 20%.
